title: Robert Monroe: the world is mined for loosh

tellings.quote: uh Monroe talks about uh the world being kind of mined for luch
He said that we're in a louch farm. That humans are being deliberately subjected to conditions that create extreme emotional states.
tellings.difference: Dates it to 1985 and cites Far Journeys, adding that humans are deliberately put into extreme emotional states.
tellings.link_reason: Both tell Robert Monroe's idea that humans are farmed, or mined, for loosh.

plain: The claim is that our world is a kind of farm, and that what gets harvested is "loosh", a word the author Robert Monroe uses for something drawn out of human feeling. Michels raises it himself, in passing, saying that Monroe talks about the world being "kind of mined" for loosh. A researcher named Jason Jorjani tells it at more length, without pointing to a page. He says Monroe described us as living in a "loosh farm". In his summary, humans are "deliberately subjected to conditions that create extreme emotional states". Jorjani credits the idea to Monroe's book Far Journeys, which he dates to 1985. So the two tellers are Michels, repeating it briefly in his own words, and a researcher who names the book and adds the point about extreme emotion being made on purpose. If true, it would mean human suffering is not an accident but something someone is farming.
